images.alt: Conceptual material flow from source through plant, haul, placement and compaction, with separate plant-return and hot-in-place recycling routes.

images.alt: The batch route shows cold-feed bins, drying and heating, screening and hot bins, weighing a batch, mixing with binder and storage. The continuous route shows proportioning, flow measurement, continuous drying and mixing with metered binder, and storage.
images.caption: Note. Adapted from The asphalt handbook (7th ed., MS-4; Figure 7.2, p. 310 / PDF 344 ; Figure 7.4, p. 312 / PDF 346 ), by Asphalt Institute, 2007. Converted equipment drawings into two simplified process lanes; omitted settings and detailed control systems. Original Figure 7.2 is credited to Terex Roadbuilding in the handbook's contributor list. Original Figure 7.4 is credited to National Highway Institute (NHI) in the handbook's contributor list. Copyright 2007 by Asphalt Institute; original contributor credits retained.

images.alt: Mixture enters the hopper, travels rearward on slat conveyors, is distributed laterally by augers and passes beneath the screed to form the mat. The diagram names functions without prescribing controls or settings.
images.caption: Note. Adapted from The asphalt handbook (7th ed., MS-4; Figure 8.11, p. 377 / PDF 411 ; 8.4.1, component descriptions, p. 378 / PDF 412 ), by Asphalt Institute, 2007. Replaced the perspective equipment schematic with a labelled functional material route. Not drawn to scale or tied to an actual model. Original Figure 8.11 is credited to Volvo Construction Equipment in the handbook's contributor list. Copyright 2007 by Asphalt Institute; original contributor credits retained.

images.alt: A simplified free-floating screed with five named factors: angle of attack, head of material, forward motion or paving speed, screed weight, and HMA stability influenced by temperature and gradation. No control setting or adjustment is specified.

images.alt: A pass counts a roller crossing over one point. Coverage concerns the full mat width. A point may receive two passes while the full width has received only one complete coverage. Three coloured bands are conceptual, not an operating pattern.
images.caption: Note. Adapted from Asphalt Institute. (2007). The asphalt handbook (7th ed., MS-4). Figure 9.1, p. 416 / PDF 450. Replaced the original five-pass pattern with separate point and full-width concepts, plus a new record-reading example. No operating pattern is prescribed.  Copyright 2007 by Asphalt Institute. ACCESS redraw (2026). Source and context .
